chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub and Fadala ibn Ayyub from Al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) about a man who had a female slave who was freed, then married, and gave birth. Is it permissible for his first master to marry her daughter? He said: No, she is forbidden to him, and she is his daughter. The free woman and the slave woman are equal in this matter.
ai.seo_question: Can a former master marry the daughter of his freed female slave?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al--Istibsar, the Imam clarifies that the prohibition of marrying a daughter extends to the daughter of a freed slave woman whom the master previously married, establishing that emancipation creates a permanent kinship bond (illa) akin to blood lineage. This ruling underscores the principle that the status of the mother (whether originally a slave or free) does not alter the prohibition for the former master, reinforcing the consistency of marital restrictions in Shia jurisprudence. The narration highlights the legal equivalence between free and enslaved women in the context of foster-kinship, a key topic in the chapter on marriage prohibitions.
